322	        service?.hasActiveAudio == true
323	    }
324	
325	    func acquire(_ service: AudioCaptureService) {
326	        if let existing = self.service, existing !== service {
327	            existing.stopForExclusiveAudioHandoff()
328	        }
329	        self.service = service
330	    }
331	
332	    func release(_ service: AudioCaptureService) {
333	        guard self.service === service else { return }

344	        interruptionObserver = center.addObserver(
345	            forName: AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification,
346	            object: AVAudioSession.sharedInstance(),
347	            queue: .main
348	        ) { [weak self] notification in
349	            guard let rawValue = notification.userInfo?[AVAudioSessionInterruptionTypeKey] as? UInt,
350	                  AVAudioSession.InterruptionType(rawValue: rawValue) == .began else { return }
351	            Task { @MainActor [weak self] in
352	                await self?.handleAudioSessionLoss(
353	                    message: String(localized: "Audio was interrupted by another app. Please try again.", bundle: .appLanguage)
354	                )
355	            }
356	        }
357	        routeChangeObserver = center.addObserver(
358	            forName: AVAudioSession.routeChangeNotification,
359	            object: AVAudioSession.sharedInstance(),
360	            queue: .main
361	        ) { [weak self] notification in
362	            guard let rawValue = notification.userInfo?[AVAudioSessionRouteChangeReasonKey] as? UInt,
363	                  AVAudioSession.RouteChangeReason(rawValue: rawValue) == .oldDeviceUnavailable else { return }
364	            Task { @MainActor [weak self] in
365	                await self?.handleAudioSessionLoss(
366	                    message: String(localized: "Audio stopped because the playback or recording device was disconnected.", bundle: .appLanguage)
367	                )

369	        }
370	        #endif
371	    }

#!/bin/zsh

set -euo pipefail

repo_root="${0:A:h:h}"
service="$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Services/AudioTranscriptionService.swift"
settings="$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Models/AIModelSettings.swift"
pane="$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Views/Components/MultimodalAudioInputView.swift"

# File transcription is orchestration of two Apple engines plus a provider
# choice — there is no pure logic to extract, so these are wiring guards. Each
# one states a defect that actually shipped, so removing the fix fails loudly
# instead of silently restoring "record and transcribe does nothing".
count_matches() {
    local pattern="$1"
    shift
    { rg -o -- "$pattern" "$@" || true; } | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

# On iOS 26/macOS 26 an uninstalled locale has no working recognizer of either
# kind. Live dictation always installed its model; file transcription did not,
# which is exactly why one worked and the other failed on the same device.
asset_install=$(count_matches 'AssetInventory' "$service")
[[ "$asset_install" -ge 2 ]] || {
    print -u2 "File transcription no longer installs the on-device speech model; found $asset_install AssetInventory references"
    exit 1
}

# The analyzer must be the primary engine where it exists — it is the only one
# whose model the app can install.
analyzer=$(count_matches 'SpeechAnalyzer|SpeechTranscriber' "$service")
[[ "$analyzer" -ge 3 ]] || {
    print -u2 "File transcription no longer uses the modern speech analyzer; found $analyzer references"
    exit 1
}

# The legacy recognizer stays as the fallback for older iOS and unsupported
# locales; losing it would strand every release below 26.
legacy=$(count_matches 'SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest' "$service")
[[ "$legacy" == "1" ]] || {
    print -u2 "The legacy URL recognizer fallback is gone; found $legacy"
    exit 1
}

# A stalled on-device pass used to burn the full two-minute timeout before the
# server retry, which reads as a hang rather than a fallback.
short_deadline=$(count_matches 'onDeviceRecognitionTimeout' "$service")
[[ "$short_deadline" -ge 2 ]] || {
    print -u2 "The on-device pass no longer has its own shorter deadline; found $short_deadline"
    exit 1
}

# Audio routing is a privacy decision. The user's selected provider must be
# honored rather than filtered away, or a recording silently uploads to a
# different account that merely happens to have a key.
honors_selection=$(count_matches 'effective\.isCloud, isAvailable\(effective\)' "$settings")
[[ "$honors_selection" == "1" ]] || {
    print -u2 "AI transcription no longer honors the selected provider; found $honors_selection"
    exit 1
}

# ...and the pane has to say where the audio goes, in words.
names_provider=$(count_matches 'Audio is sent to' "$pane")
[[ "$names_provider" == "1" ]] || {
    print -u2 "The audio pane no longer names the provider the recording is sent to; found $names_provider"
    exit 1
}

# A first-run model download can take minutes; without progress the pane looks
# hung on exactly the run doing the most work.
download_progress=$(count_matches 'modelDownloadProgress' "$service" "$pane")
[[ "$download_progress" -ge 4 ]] || {
    print -u2 "Speech-model download progress is no longer surfaced; found $download_progress references"
    exit 1
}

# Every string this feature introduced must carry a translation, or the 中文
# interface reverts to English on the screen explaining where audio is sent.
python3 - "$repo_root/SwiftMandarin/Localizable.xcstrings" <<'PY'
import json
import sys

with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    strings = json.load(handle)["strings"]

required = [
    "The on-device speech model for %@ could not be downloaded: %@. Check your network connection and try again, or switch to an AI transcription provider.",
    "AI transcription needs a cloud provider. Add an API key in Settings → AI, or switch back to Apple Speech.",
    "Audio is sent to %@.",
    "Downloading the %@ speech model…",
    "Speech model download",
    "speech-to-text model id",
]

missing = []
for key in required:
    unit = (
        strings.get(key, {})
        .get("localizations", {})
        .get("zh-Hans", {})
        .get("stringUnit", {})
    )
    if unit.get("state") != "translated" or not unit.get("value"):
        missing.append(key)

if missing:
    sys.stderr.write("Transcription strings are missing a zh-Hans translation (%d):\n" % len(missing))
    for key in missing[:5]:
        sys.stderr.write("  %r\n" % key)
    sys.exit(1)
PY

print "Audio transcription wiring checks passed (8/8)"

### 1) Request & Context

> "for the multimodal tab feature, for the audio portion of record and transcribe audio, it doesnt work. why isnt it set to the same audio model as the selected audio model. also, the default apple speech recognition model doesnt work. fix these"

Two independent defects behind one symptom, both confirmed by reading the code rather than guessed at.

### 2) Root cause A — file transcription never installed a speech model

`SpeechRecognitionService` (live dictation) and `AudioTranscriptionService` (record/import, the Multimodal tab) had diverged. The live path had already been modernized: on iOS 26 / macOS 26 it uses `SpeechAnalyzer` + `SpeechTranscriber`, and — the part that matters — it calls `AssetInventory.assetInstallationRequest` to **download the locale's recognition model** before recognizing anything.

The file path did neither. It used only `SFSpeechRecognizer` + `SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest` and installed nothing:

```
$ grep -c AssetInventory Services/SpeechRecognitionService.swift   # 1
$ grep -c AssetInventory Services/AudioTranscriptionService.swift  # 0
```

On these releases recognition assets are managed by `AssetInventory`, so a locale whose model has never been downloaded has no working recognizer of *either* kind. `SFSpeechRecognizer.isAvailable` then stays false, and the file path's three-second availability poll gives up with "Apple Speech has no recognizer available for …". That is exactly the reported shape: live dictation works, record-and-transcribe does not, on the same device.

**Fix.** `AudioTranscriptionService` now runs `SpeechAnalyzer` + `SpeechTranscriber` first — installing the locale's model when it is missing, with download progress surfaced in the pane — and keeps `SFSpeechRecognizer` for iOS 17–25 and as the fallback when the analyzer cannot serve the locale (its server pass can still read audio the on-device model returned nothing for). When both fail on OS 26 the analyzer's error is reported, because the legacy engine's "no recognizer available" is a symptom of the same missing model and would send the user hunting in the wrong place.

Two smaller repairs came with it. The on-device pass now has its own 20-second deadline instead of sharing the 120-second one: a stalled first attempt used to delay the server retry by two minutes, which reads as a hang rather than a fallback. And a first-run model download reports progress, so the slowest run is no longer the one that looks dead.

### 3) Root cause B — AI transcription ignored the selected provider

`transcriptionProvider()` filtered the user's own selection through `supportsAudioTranscription`, which is true for exactly OpenAI, Qwen, and Quotio:

```swift
if effective.supportsAudioTranscription, isAvailable(effective) { return effective }
return AIProvider.allCases.first { $0.supportsAudioTranscription && isAvailable($0) }
```

So a learner whose selected provider was Zhipu, MiniMax, DeepSeek, Claude, or Doubao did not get their selection. Their recording was uploaded to whichever *other* provider they happened to hold a key for — silently, with only a small brand icon to hint at it — or the feature refused outright. Silently choosing where a recording is uploaded is the one thing this decision must never do.

**Fix.** The selection comes first: any configured cloud provider is used as chosen, and the documented-endpoint list now only picks the *fallback* and the curated model ids. This matches the intent already written into `supportsAudioTranscription`'s own comment — that the base URL and model are user-editable and "a provider that turns out not to serve the route answers with its own HTTP error, which is surfaced verbatim rather than hidden". The pane now states in words which provider the audio goes to, and says plainly when the selected one is outside the documented set.

| Requirement | Check | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| R31.1 Apple Speech transcribes a recorded clip | File path installs the locale model and uses the analyzer | `test-audio-transcription.sh`; mutation test T1 |
| R31.2 Older iOS keeps working | `SFSpeechURLRecognitionRequest` fallback retained | wiring check |
| R31.3 A stalled on-device pass falls back promptly | On-device deadline is separate and shorter | wiring check; mutation test T3 |
| R31.4 Audio goes to the provider the user selected | `transcriptionProvider()` honors the selection | wiring check; mutation test T2 |
| R31.5 The destination is stated, not implied | Pane names the provider in words | wiring check; mutation test T4 |
| R31.6 A model download is not mistaken for a hang | Progress surfaced in the pane | wiring check |
| R31.7 The feature reads in 中文 | 7 new keys translated | catalog check |

### 5) Verification Summary

- `zsh init.sh` green — 191/191 MiniMax, 27/27 audio-session, 173/173 AI prompt, 29/29 provider wiring, 28/28 learning-direction, 8/8 direction wiring, 556/556 auto-analysis queue, 9/9 auto-analysis wiring, and the new 8/8 transcription wiring checks.

- Mutation testing (4/4 caught): removing the asset install, restoring the old provider gate, dropping the shorter on-device deadline, and removing the provider name each fail the suite. All restored and re-verified.
- **Localization coverage is now checked correctly, and the earlier check was not.** The Iteration 30 sweep parsed `.stringsdata` `tables` as a dictionary; Xcode writes it as an *array* of `{key, comment, location}` records, so the comparison matched nothing and "0 missing, 0 untranslated" was vacuous. Re-run with a parser that handles both shapes over all 1,219 extracted keys: every key added in Iterations 30 and 31 is present and translated. The only remaining gaps are pre-existing and benign — ten `${applicationName}` App Intents phrases (handled by AppShortcuts, not the catalog), eleven punctuation/format-scaffolding keys with no words in them, and five deliberately bilingual keys whose Chinese localization drops the English clause.

### 6) Remaining Work & Next Steps

- **No device run.** The analyzer path is asserted through the SDK's declared API and a clean build on both platforms; it has not been exercised against a real recording, and the model download in particular has not been watched end to end.
- **Provider ASR support is still documentation-derived.** OpenAI is certain; Qwen and Quotio were asserted from documentation in Iteration 28 and remain unverified. content.text:
Both defects are fixed. They were separate causes behind the one symptom.

## Why Apple Speech didn't work

The two speech paths had diverged. Live dictation was modernized to `SpeechAnalyzer`/`SpeechTranscriber` and — the part that matters — calls `AssetInventory` to **download the locale's on-device model** before recognizing. File transcription did neither:

```bash
grep -c AssetInventory SwiftMandarin/Services/SpeechRecognitionService.swift SwiftMandarin/Services/AudioTranscriptionService.swift
```

That returned `1` and `0`. On iOS 26 / macOS 26 recognition assets are managed by `AssetInventory`, so a locale whose model was never downloaded has no working recognizer of *either* kind — `SFSpeechRecognizer.isAvailable` stays false and the 3-second availability poll gives up with "no recognizer available". Exactly the shape you saw: dictation works, record-and-transcribe doesn't, same device.

[AudioTranscriptionService.swift](SwiftMandarin/Services/AudioTranscriptionService.swift) now runs the analyzer first, installing the model when missing, and keeps `SFSpeechRecognizer` for iOS 17–25 and for locales the analyzer can't serve. Two related repairs: the on-device pass got its own 20-second deadline (a stall used to delay the server retry by two minutes, which reads as a hang), and a first-run model download now shows progress instead of looking dead.

## Why it wasn't using your selected model

`transcriptionProvider()` filtered *your own selection* through `supportsAudioTranscription` — true for only OpenAI, Qwen, and Quotio:

```swift
if effective.supportsAudioTranscription, isAvailable(effective) { return effective }
return AIProvider.allCases.first { $0.supportsAudioTranscription && isAvailable($0) }
```

So if your selected provider was Zhipu, MiniMax, DeepSeek, Claude, or Doubao, your recording was uploaded to whichever *other* provider you happened to hold a key for — silently, with only a small brand icon as a hint — or refused outright. Now the selection wins; the documented-endpoint list only picks the fallback and the curated model ids. This matches the intent already written in that flag's own comment (a provider that doesn't serve the route answers with its own error, surfaced verbatim). The pane also now states in words which provider the audio goes to.

## Verification

- `zsh init.sh` green, including a new **8/8** transcription wiring suite; **4/4 mutation tests** caught their defect (removing the asset install, restoring the old provider gate, dropping the shorter deadline, removing the provider name).
- macOS and iOS Simulator Debug builds: `BUILD SUCCEEDED`, zero warnings, zero errors.
- 7 new strings translated to zh-Hans.

One correction to my previous turn: the `.stringsdata` coverage check I cited as evidence parsed `tables` as a dictionary, but Xcode writes an array — so it matched nothing and its "0 missing" was vacuous. Re-run with a parser handling both shapes across all 1,219 extracted keys: every key from both changes is present and translated, so the conclusion held. Remaining catalog gaps are pre-existing and benign (App Intents `${applicationName}` phrases, punctuation scaffolding, and deliberately bilingual keys).

Not done: no device run and no live provider call — the analyzer path is asserted from the SDK's declared API and clean builds, not from a real recording. Qwen/Quotio ASR support remains documentation-derived; the change makes that honest rather than resolved.

--- c290b39a2b70118f1a73c23d1da7160f37dc145a
Let Xcode normalize the string catalog

The Release builds rewrote Localizable.xcstrings. The diff is large but the
content is unchanged apart from two corrections Xcode made on its own:

- The superseded English app-description key is now marked extractionState
  "stale". Its copy was replaced in AboutView, so nothing references it any
  more, and the marker is what tells a translator to stop maintaining it.
- The ", " separator key picked up the comment written at its call site in
  VocabularyImportExportService, which explains to a translator that it joins
  the clauses of the import summary.

Everything else is re-ordering. The 89 keys added by script in an earlier
commit were appended at the end of the file; Xcode has filed them into its own
collation order. Key set, translations, sourceLanguage and version are all
identical — verified by comparing the two documents entry by entry.

--- 6aaf9ad9c8855f27e78e3522cfb278c9342aad2e
Document the two learning directions, ship v4.2.0 DMG

READMEs. Both now describe the app as two-directional rather than a Mandarin
course with a translated interface. The English README's tagline and overview
still framed it as "Your Complete Mandarin Chinese Learning Companion" — the
Chinese README had already moved on — and neither explained what the reverse
mode actually does. Both gain a "Two Learning Directions" section with a table
comparing the two side by side: which word takes the headline, pinyin versus
IPA, which language the AI explains in, which side the tappable reader
annotates, which language leads the narration, and that tone drills are hidden
for a native Mandarin reader because there is nothing there to train. The
Settings list now says the learner mode re-orients the whole app, and that the
pinyin display options only appear for someone learning Chinese.

Version. MARKETING_VERSION was 3.0, the newest release tag was v4.1.0, and the
shipped DMG was named 2.0 — three numbers for one app. All three are now 4.2:
MARKETING_VERSION 4.2, CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION 42, and the DMG named for it.

DMG. dist/ carried a 1.7 MB build from an older tree; it is replaced with a
fresh 5.5 MB Release build of the current code, plus its sha256. Verified by
mounting the image, copying the app out, and launching it.

--- ad848f203d13622adbe22904a7a7d68998135e41
Fix two build errors the local type-check harness missed

Both come from the previous commit and both fail `xcodebuild`.

AppPreferences.init seeded the shared defaultDirection key by reading
self.learnerMode, which is a `self` access before every stored property is
initialized. It compiled under a bare `swiftc -typecheck` because @Observable
had not expanded there — that macro is what turns learnerMode into a computed
access in the first place. The resolved mode is now held in a local and the
seed reads that.

LanguageBundleOverride's members were implicitly main-actor-isolated, because
the target builds with SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor, while
`appLanguage` is explicitly nonisolated and `localizedString(forKey:value:table:)`
overrides a nonisolated ObjC method. Every member of the extension is now
explicitly nonisolated, which is what the file always needed: it is reached
from `String(localized:bundle:)` calls throughout the models and services.

Also corrects handoff.md. It claimed the app "type-checks with zero errors"
and that Xcode was unavailable. Xcode is installed at /Applications/Xcode-beta.app
— only xcode-select pointed elsewhere, and the check scripts' own DEVELOPER_DIR
default had been saying so all along. The harness that produced that claim was
then shown to be untrustworthy by reverting both fixes and watching it still
report clean: `swiftc -typecheck` skips SIL diagnostic passes and never loads
the macro plugins.

Verified with the real compiler this time: macOS Debug and generic iOS
Simulator Debug both BUILD SUCCEEDED with zero errors and zero warnings, and
init.sh is green at 456 assertions.

cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rogerlin-Downloads-SwiftMandarin-main/ae56111d-7374-4136-bc40-16625f9b5feb/scratchpad/msg.txt <<'MSG'
Analyze saved words automatically, and repair audio transcription

Two changes that both touch AIModelSettings and the string catalog, so they
land together.

Auto-translate new words. The Batch AI Analysis menu gains an opt-in
"Auto-Translate New Words" toggle: every word or phrase saved to the vocabulary
list is translated and analyzed in the background by the selected provider,
instead of waiting for a reviewed batch run. AutoAnalysisCoordinator resolves
the headword, reading, and gloss exactly the way BatchExplanationController
does and writes to the same WordExplanationCacheStore key, so the automatic and
manual runs never repeat each other's work and the screen's "Needs Analysis"
count falls on its own. One notification in SavedTermsStore.add covers every
capture surface — Translate, photos, the reader, the menu bar, Shortcuts, and
import — so no path can be added later that quietly opts out.

Because this spends tokens with nobody watching, the rules that bound it live
in AutoAnalysisQueue, a Foundation-only value with no app dependencies: one
request per word (folded on the same key the vocabulary and cache stores use),
at most 500 words waiting with overflow refused and counted rather than
evicting accepted work, at most three dispatches per word, and both queue
halves persisted so a request interrupted by quitting resumes at the next
launch instead of vanishing. The coordinator adds the rest: off by default,
yields to a running reviewed batch rather than doubling the request rate,
pauses itself after three consecutive failures instead of re-billing a broken
endpoint once per saved word, refuses to cache a response that came back under
settings that changed mid-flight, and never touches the paid MiniMax speech
pipeline.

Audio transcription. Record-and-transcribe in the Multimodal tab did not work,
for two unrelated reasons.

The first is that file transcription never installed a speech model. Live
dictation had been modernized to SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber and calls
AssetInventory to download the locale's on-device model; AudioTranscriptionService
still used only SFSpeechRecognizer and installed nothing (grep -c AssetInventory
returned 1 and 0). On iOS 26 and macOS 26 those assets are what a recognizer
needs, so a locale that was never downloaded has no working recognizer of
either kind: isAvailable stays false and the three-second poll gives up with
"Apple Speech has no recognizer available". That is why dictation worked and
record-and-transcribe failed on the same device. The analyzer is now the
primary file engine, installing the model when it is missing and reporting
download progress in the pane; SFSpeechRecognizer stays for iOS 17-25 and for
locales the analyzer cannot serve, since its server pass can still read audio
the on-device model returned nothing for. The on-device pass also gets its own
20-second deadline — sharing the 120-second one meant a stalled first attempt
delayed the server retry by two minutes, which reads as a hang rather than a
fallback.

The second is that AI transcription ignored the selected provider.
transcriptionProvider() filtered the user's own choice through
supportsAudioTranscription, true for exactly OpenAI, Qwen, and Quotio, so a
learner on Zhipu, MiniMax, DeepSeek, Claude, or Doubao had their recording
uploaded to whichever other provider they happened to hold a key for — silently,
with only a brand icon as a hint — or was refused outright. The selection now
wins, and the documented-endpoint list only picks the fallback and the curated
model ids. This is what the flag's own comment already intended: the base URL
and model are user-editable, and a provider that does not serve the route
answers with its own HTTP error, surfaced verbatim. The pane now also names, in
words, the provider a recording will be sent to.

Verification. init.sh is green and gains two suites: 556 auto-analysis queue
contracts plus 9 wiring guards, and 8 transcription wiring guards. Nine
mutation tests confirm the guards fail when a save hook, the retry bound, the
batch yield, the no-audio rule, the asset install, the provider fix, the
shorter deadline, a provider name, or a translation is removed. macOS and
generic iOS Simulator Debug both BUILD SUCCEEDED with zero errors and zero
warnings. All 24 new strings carry zh-Hans translations, verified against
Xcode's own extracted .stringsdata across all 1,219 keys — with a corrected
parser, since the first one read the tables as a dictionary where Xcode writes
an array and so had been comparing nothing.

Not done: no device run and no live provider call. The queue's behavior against
a real endpoint under rate limiting, and the analyzer against a real recording,
are asserted through contracts and the shared provider path rather than
observed.
MSG
